overview: An amino acid is a single building block; a protein is the large, folded molecule built by linking many of them together.
genZNote: Amino acid is one Lego brick. Protein is the finished Lego castle.

aspects.label: Unit vs Polymer
aspects.valueA: A single monomer unit containing an amino group, carboxyl group, and side chain (R group).
aspects.valueB: A polymer of many amino acids joined by peptide bonds, folded into a specific 3D structure.

aspects.label: Diversity
aspects.valueB: Virtually unlimited combinations, since sequence and folding create huge structural diversity.

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: Serves as the raw material and, individually, as some signalling molecules or neurotransmitter precursors.
aspects.valueB: Performs the actual biological function: catalysis, structure, transport, defence, etc.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A protein's specific function depends on its 3D folded shape, which is ultimately dictated by its amino acid sequence.
overlay.memoryTrick: Amino acids are letters; a protein is the whole sentence they spell out.
overlay.commonMisconception: A chain of amino acids is not automatically a functional protein — it must fold correctly into its native 3D shape first.
